title_en: Wonders of Chinese Engineering (4/20): The Shanghai Tower
note_en: A number in Chinese often comes straight after the verb to say how much something changed: 旋转了一百二十度 "twisted 120 degrees," 降低了百分之二十四 "was cut by 24 percent." English usually needs "by" here, but Chinese simply puts verb + 了 + amount; adding 了 marks the change as complete.

sentences.en: At this point Amira closed her laptop and thought: since its completion in 2015, the Shanghai Tower's height record has never been beaten in China, while the world record is still held by the Burj Khalifa in her hometown of Dubai. Yet the 270 wind turbines at the top of this Shanghai tower, originally expected to supply about 10 percent of its electricity, actually produce far less than planned, only about 54,000 kilowatt-hours a year, enough just for the exterior lighting. Even the building with the most records, she couldn't help thinking, has its ordinary side that sets no records at all.
